pages.title: Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 — removal of arrested Ministers

facts.text: Introduced: in Lok Sabha by the Union Home Minister
facts.head: News

facts.text: Amends: Article 75 (Council of Ministers incl. PM)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Provision: a Minister arrested and detained for 30 consecutive days on allegation of an offence punishable with 5 years or more imprisonment shall be removed by the President on the advice of the PM by the 31st day
facts.head: News

facts.text: Applies to: both Union and State Ministers
facts.head: News

facts.text: UTs: separate amendments to Government of Union Territories Act, 1963 and J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019
facts.head: News

facts.text: Backdrop: V. Senthil Balaji case (2023), Tamil Nadu — Minister continued in office despite arrest in money-laundering case
facts.head: News

facts.text: ⚠ Not limited to Union Ministers — applies to State Ministers too
facts.head: News

facts.text: Bills: Government of UTs (Amendment) Bill, 2025; J&K Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2025; Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025 (same session)
facts.head: Related bills and procedure

facts.text: Rules waived: Rule 19A (prior notice before introduction) and Rule 19B (advance circulation to MPs) of Lok Sabha
facts.head: Related bills and procedure

facts.text: Reason: Monsoon Session ending 21 August 2025
facts.head: Related bills and procedure

facts.text: Critic: Congress MP Abhishek Singhvi — could be weaponised by "biased central agencies"
facts.head: Related bills and procedure

facts.text: Article 75: Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Article 164(1): State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Constitution did not explicitly bar Ministers in detention from holding office
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Covers: PM, Chief Ministers, Union and State Ministers — custody 30 consecutive days without bail
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

facts.text: Removal by: President (PM/Union Ministers) or Governor (CM/State Ministers) on advice of the executive head
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

facts.text: Automatic cessation: if advice not tendered by the 31st day, the person automatically ceases to be Minister
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

facts.text: Re-appointment: allowed after release from custody under Article 75(1)
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

facts.text: ⚠ No permanent disqualification — can be re-appointed
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

facts.text: Three bills: Govt of UTs (Amendment), Constitution (130th Amendment), J&K Reorganisation (Amendment) — all 2025
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

facts.text: JPC: 31 members — 21 Lok Sabha + 10 Rajya Sabha; report by the Winter Session
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

facts.text: JPC background: ad hoc body of both Houses; can summon officials and documents; recommendations not binding
facts.head: More provisions and JPC

pages.title: Section 152 BNS — sedition debate and press freedom

facts.text: Event: Assam Police summoned The Wire founding editor Siddharth Varadarajan and consulting editor Karan Thapar under Section 152 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Related to: coverage of Operation Sindoor
facts.head: News

facts.text: Same day: Supreme Court issued notice on The Wire's petition challenging Section 152 and protected journalists from coercive action
facts.head: News

facts.text: Lapses: summons lacked FIR date, offence details, FIR copy — against BNSS provisions
facts.head: News

facts.text: Section 152 BNS: seen as rebranded Section 124A IPC (sedition) — SC kept 124A in abeyance in 2022
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Covers: acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India; vague term "knowingly"
facts.head: Background

facts.text: ⚠ Unlike 124A, Section 152 does not demand a high standard of proof of intent
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Right involved: Article 19(1)(a) — freedom of speech and expression
facts.head: Background

pages.title: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025

facts.text: Passed: Lok Sabha by voice vote, Monsoon Session
facts.head: News

facts.text: Bans: offering, operation, facilitation, advertisement, promotion and participation in online money games (fantasy sports, card games with stakes)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Promotes: e-sports and recreational/social gaming — through a regulatory authority
facts.head: News

facts.text: Not released for public consultation — govt: prohibition laws need no public debate
facts.head: News

facts.text: Persons: Speaker Om Birla; IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw; IT Secretary S. Krishnan
facts.head: News

facts.text: Became law: 22 August 2025 after Presidential assent
facts.head: News

facts.text: Category: E-sports; Detail: recognised under National Sports Governance Act, 2025; registration; entry fee allowed, performance-based prizes (e.g. Call of Duty, GTA competitive)
facts.head: Classification of games

facts.text: Category: Online social games; Detail: casual/educational; no betting; promoted by govt
facts.head: Classification of games

facts.text: Category: Real Money Games (RMGs); Detail: stake money/tokens for monetary reward (poker, rummy, fantasy sports, paid ludo) — completely banned
facts.head: Classification of games

facts.text: Offering RMGs / fund transactions: up to 3 years jail, fine up to ₹1 crore
facts.head: Penalties and institutions

facts.text: Advertising RMGs: up to 2 years, fine up to ₹50 lakh
facts.head: Penalties and institutions

facts.text: Offences: cognisable and non-bailable (BNSS 2023)
facts.head: Penalties and institutions

facts.text: Blocking: CERT-In; Interpol for foreign operators
facts.head: Penalties and institutions

facts.text: ⚠ No penalty for players — only operators/advertisers
facts.head: Penalties and institutions

facts.text: Regulatory Authority; funds from Consolidated Fund of India for social gaming
facts.head: Penalties and institutions

facts.text: Earlier: IT Rules, 2021 amendments (2023) — KYC, parental controls, age rating
facts.head: Penalties and institutions

facts.text: Losses: ~₹15,000 crore a year to RMGs; 32 gaming suicides in Karnataka in 31 months
facts.head: Data and issues

facts.text: Fraud cited: ₹400 crore via Chinese app FIEWIN; ₹30,000 crore GST evasion; ₹2,000 crore tax evasion (2022)
facts.head: Data and issues

facts.text: Constitution: betting & gambling — Entries 34 & 62, State List
facts.head: Data and issues

facts.text: GST: uniform 28% on entry fee/deposit (2023) — SC stayed notices
facts.head: Data and issues

facts.text: Challenge ground: Article 19(1)(g) — skill vs chance
facts.head: Data and issues

facts.text: Industry: 2 lakh jobs, 400+ firms
facts.head: Data and issues

facts.text: ⚠ Act has no explicit child-protection provisions
facts.head: Data and issues

facts.text: Amends: Indian Institutes of Management Act, 2017
facts.head: News

facts.text: Creates: 22nd IIM at Guwahati, Assam
facts.head: News

facts.text: Outlay: ₹555 crore
facts.head: News

facts.text: Admissions: from 2025-26 (Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Passed: Lok Sabha 19 August 2025; Rajya Sabha 20 August 2025 (Opposition absent — demanded discussion on Bihar SIR)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Item: First IIM; Detail: 1961
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Item: Before 2014; Detail: 13 IIMs in 53 years
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Item: After 2014; Detail: 9 new IIMs
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Rolls: over 99 crore entries; EC shares them as image PDFs (no voter photos)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Database: ERONET — EC's digital application for voter details; rolls prepared by district officials
facts.head: News

facts.text: Example: Congress manually found 11,965 duplicate entries in Mahadevapura (Bengaluru)
facts.head: News

facts.text: EC stand: before 2019 elections, EC told CEOs to stop uploading machine-readable rolls (prevent foreign access)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Case: Kamal Nath vs EC of India (2018) — SC refused to compel EC to give machine-readable rolls; citizens may use OCR
facts.head: News

facts.text: Scale: over 6 crore pages nationwide
facts.head: News

facts.text: Persons: activist P.G. Bhat; transparency advocate Srinivas Kodali; Rahul Gandhi
facts.head: News

pages.title: Presidential Reference under Article 143 on timelines for assent to Bills

facts.text: Reference by: President Droupadi Murmu — can President and Governors be judicially compelled to act within timelines on State Bills?
facts.head: News

facts.text: Bench: Constitution Bench led by CJI B.R. Gavai
facts.head: News

facts.text: Trigger: SC judgment of 8 April 2025 — Justices J.B. Pardiwala and R. Mahadevan
facts.head: News

facts.text: Tamil Nadu Governor R.N. Ravi's delay on 10 re-passed Bills held illegal
facts.head: News

facts.text: ⚠ First time judicially enforceable timelines imposed on Governors and President
facts.head: News

facts.text: 143(1): President may refer a question of law or fact of public importance for advisory opinion
facts.head: Background — Article 143

facts.text: 143(2): disputes on pre-Constitution treaties, agreements
facts.head: Background — Article 143

facts.text: Opinion: advisory, not binding (but persuasive)
facts.head: Background — Article 143

facts.text: ⚠ SC cannot directly overrule its own precedent in a Reference — can only clarify or suggest a larger bench
facts.head: Background — Article 143
